documents.abstract: This study examined the role of Artificial Intelligence-Supported Sustainable Education in promoting students’ Environmental Learning Engagement, with particular focus on the moderating role of Environmental Self-Efficacy. A quantitative cross-sectional research design was used, and data were collected from 389 university students in Pakistan through an adopted structured questionnaire administered online using Google Forms. The collected responses were organized in Microsoft Excel and subsequently analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics. Pearson Product-Moment Correlation, simple linear regression, and moderation analysis were used to examine the relationships among the study variables. The findings showed that Artificial Intelligence-Supported Sustainable Education was positively associated with Environmental Learning Engagement and significantly predicted students’ engagement in environmental learning. The findings further indicated that Environmental Self-Efficacy significantly strengthened the relationship between AI-supported sustainable education and environmental learning engagement. These findings suggest that AI-supported educational environments can provide students with accessible, interactive, and sustainability-focused learning opportunities that may encourage greater participation in environmental learning. The study further highlights that technological support may be more effective when students possess confidence in their ability to understand environmental issues and participate in environmentally relevant learning activities. The study contributes to the emerging literature by connecting AI-supported sustainable education with environmental learning engagement while incorporating Environmental Self-Efficacy as an important individual-level factor. The findings may assist educators, higher education institutions, and policymakers in developing technology-supported sustainable learning environments that encourage active participation, environmental understanding, and meaningful student engagement.

Abstract Background Accurate assessment of tumor invasion depth is essential for treatment selection in rectal cancer. Transrectal ultrasound (TRUS) provides high-resolution visualization of rectal wall layers but is highly operator-dependent, limiting reproducibility outside expert centers. Artificial intelligence–based approaches may help standardize TRUS interpretation, particularly for depth-of-invasion assessment. Methods We developed and evaluated a two-stage deep learning model for automated analysis of standard TRUS images. A total of 677 two-dimensional images from 103 patients were included. In Stage 1, images were classified as normal or cancer. Images identified as cancer were then analyzed in Stage 2 to classify invasion depth as superficial (T0–T1) or deep (T2–T4). Models were trained using transfer learning with five-fold cross-validation and evaluated on an independent held-out test set. Performance was assessed using accuracy, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and class-specific recall. Results On the independent test set, the two-stage pipeline achieved an overall three-class accuracy of 82.4%. Stage 1 discriminated normal from cancer with an accuracy of 89.7% and an AUC of 0.93, ensuring reliable identification of tumor-containing images. Among cancer-positive images, Stage 2 differentiated superficial from deep invasion with an accuracy of 85.6% and an AUC of 0.91. Performance was consistent across the dataset and comparable to reported accuracies of expert-performed TRUS. Conclusions A two-stage deep learning approach applied to standard TRUS images enables automated, practice-oriented classification of rectal tumor invasion depth. By reflecting real-world diagnostic workflows and reducing operator dependence, this method may support more consistent TRUS-based staging and assist treatment decision-making, particularly in nonspecialized centers.

Objective To compare radiographic osteotomy healing scores after tibial plateau leveling osteotomy (TPLO) in young (2–5 years) and old (8–12 years) dogs using the modified Radiographic Union Score for Tibial fractures (mRUST) system, and to evaluate agreement between large language model-assisted interpretation (LLM), surgeon, and surgical resident scoring. Study design Client-owned, 20–40 kg dogs treated with unilateral TPLO at ages 2–5 or 8–12 years between 2023 and 2025 were retrospectively identified. Dogs with endocrinopathy or atypical TPLO or recovery were excluded. Dogs were assigned to Group 1 (2–5 years) or Group 2 (8–12 years). 8-week postoperative radiographs were scored independently by an LLM, a surgeon, and a surgical resident using the 4-point mRUST system. Scores were compared between age groups using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test, and interrater agreement was assessed using an intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Results Group 1 had 49 dogs; Group 2 had 51 dogs. Group 1 had a mean (SD) age of 3.82 (1.11) years, while Group 2 had a mean (SD) age of 9.24 (0.99) years. mRUST scores did not differ between age groups across LLM ( p = 0.352), surgeon ( p = 0.908), or resident assessments ( p = 0.588). LLM, surgeon, and resident scores had only fair agreement (ICC = 0.4504, p < 0.001). Conclusion Chronological age was not associated with mRUST score following TPLO at the 8-week postoperative evaluation. The mRUST system demonstrated moderate agreement between human observers. LLM scoring showed promise; further refinement is needed for clinical application.

BACKGROUND: Presenteeism is an occupational health challenge. Although adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) have been linked to adult health, evidence on comprehensive ACE exposure and presenteeism remains limited. METHODS: We analyzed data from working adults in the 2022 Japan COVID-19 and Society Internet Survey (JACSIS). ACEs were assessed using an expanded Japanese ACE questionnaire and categorized as 0, 1, 2, 3, and ≥4 ACEs. Presenteeism was measured using the Work Functioning Impairment Scale (WFun), and high presenteeism was defined as WFun ≥21. Using logistic regression, we examined the association between ACE counts (0, 1, 2, 3, and ≥4) and high presenteeism. We further evaluated the cumulative effect of increasing ACE counts. Models were adjusted for age, sex, educational attainment, marital status, weekly working hours, and job stress. Stratified analyses were conducted by current mental disorder status. RESULTS: Among 19,409 workers included in the analytic sample, those with any ACE exposure had higher odds of high presenteeism than those reporting no ACEs, and the association displayed a dose-response pattern with increasing ACE counts. This graded relationship was also observed in stratified analyses, irrespective of the presence or absence of a current mental disorder. CONCLUSIONS: This study suggests that expanded childhood adversity is relevant to presenteeism among working adults, regardless of current mental disorder status. These findings reveal the value of a life-course perspective in occupational health and point to the need for future research to clarify the mechanisms linking ACE exposure to presenteeism and to examine trauma-informed approaches for reducing presenteeism.

documents.abstract: Abstract Background Thyroid fine-needle aspiration cytology is widely used to evaluate thyroid nodules before surgery. Recent advances in deep learning have increased the potential for artificial intelligence-assisted cytological diagnosis. However, developing accurate models usually requires large numbers of images labelled by experts, making dataset preparation time-consuming and costly. We investigate whether self-supervised learning can improve thyroid cytology image classification while reducing the need for labelled data. Methods We retrospectively analysed cytology images from 393 thyroid nodules and extracted 142,158 image patches. Three self-supervised learning methods were used to pre-train vision transformer models on unlabelled images, followed by classification training with different amounts of labelled data. Performance in classifying eight lesion types was assessed using five-fold cross-validation, precision–recall area under the curve, and macro-averaged F1 scores. Model performance was compared with ImageNet-pretrained models and four cytotechnologists. Results Here we show that self-supervised learning maintains high classification performance when labelled training data are limited and consistently outperforms ImageNet pre-training. With 1% of the labelled data, the best self-supervised model achieves a precision–recall area under the curve of 0.899, compared with 0.707 for ImageNet pre-training. The diagnostic pipeline achieves an average class-specific accuracy of 0.94, exceeding that of the four participating cytotechnologists. Self-supervised image representations also form lesion-specific clusters without diagnostic labels. Conclusions Self-supervised learning enables accurate classification of thyroid cytology images while substantially reducing the need for expert annotation. This approach may facilitate the development of more efficient artificial intelligence-assisted cytology systems, although validation using data from multiple institutions is needed.

documents.abstract: Abstract Background The Bergmann-Kliesch Score is a histopathological grading system used to evaluate spermatogenesis in testicular biopsies, quantifying the fraction of seminiferous tubules containing elongated spermatids. It serves as a key parameter in the clinical process of men with non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) undergoing testicular sperm extraction (TESE) for subsequent intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI). Manual Bergmann-Kliesch Score assessment is time-consuming and subject to inter- and intraobserver variability. This study aimed to develop and validate an artificial intelligence (AI)-based computational pipeline for automated Bergmann-Kliesch Score assessment from digitized testicular biopsy whole-slide images (WSIs). Results A retrospective monocentric cohort of 74 patients who underwent TESE at the University Medical Center Frankfurt was analyzed. A dual-model machine-learning pipeline was used to process paired haematoxylin-eosin (HE) and OCT3/4 immunohistochemically stained WSIs. A U-Net architecture with a ResNet-34 backbone was trained on 60 HE-stained slides for tubular segmentation, monitored by a multi-class Dice coefficient of 0.897 on the validation set. A second U-Net model with a ResNet-34 backbone was trained on 15 OCT3/4-stained slides comprising 14,226 manually annotated elongated spermatids for spermatid detection. Both modalities were integrated via multimodal image registration combining rigid alignment and B-spline warping, enabling spatial projection of spermatid detections onto tubular segmentations. On the patient-level held-out test set of 15 patients, AI-derived Bergmann-Kliesch Scores showed strong agreement with pathologist-assigned reference scores (Pearson r = 0.957, Spearman ρ = 0.856, R 2 = 0.916, mean absolute error = 0.93, root mean squared error = 1.28). At the clinical cutoff of Bergmann-Kliesch Score ≥ 1, the pipeline correctly classified all test-set cases. Across the full evaluation cohort of 74 patients, agreement remained robust (Pearson r = 0.851, Spearman ρ = 0.829, mean absolute error = 1.52, root mean squared error = 2.20). Conclusions This AI-based pipeline enables automated, reproducible Bergmann-Kliesch Score assessment from routinely stained testicular biopsy WSIs, demonstrating strong agreement with manual pathologist evaluation. The system shows promise as a clinical decision-support tool in TESE workflows. External multicentric validation and prospective correlation with ICSI outcome data are warranted in future studies.

documents.abstract: Introduction: The inclusion of a surgical robot as a team member adds yet another level of intricacy to the already complex environment and roles for perioperative nurses. Over the last twenty years, robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) has gained popularity due to its many benefits, including operative precision, decreased length of stay, and reduced blood loss. Aim: This discussion paper aims to provide a greater understanding of robotic surgery for perioperative nurses by offering an overview of the incidence and types of intraoperative robotic surgical emergencies and some technical and non-technical responses to these emergency situations. Discussion: Like all surgical procedures, RAS has inherent risks, with adverse surgical emergencies creating stress, ‘automation angst’, for the perioperative team members, particularly those who are not familiar or well-practiced with these procedures. Following thematic analysis of the reviewed literature, this discussion will be presented under the emerging themes, namely, ‘Robotic surgical emergencies’, ‘Non-technical skills for the multidisciplinary team’, ‘Simulation-based training for crisis management’, and ‘Implications for perioperative nurses’. Conclusion: While robotic surgical emergencies are not common, they do occur, and perioperative nurses need to be prepared. During emergency situations, communication must be at a premium, and the lessons from human factors and situational awareness are well documented. An ongoing message running through the literature was surrounding the need for education, emphasising that continuous education is required to achieve competence of surgical team members in preparing for emergency situations. Simulation may play an important role in this education. Also important will be the development and implementation of an emergency robotic undocking protocol (ERUP) to guide the team when conversion to open or speedy access to the patient is required.

Since its introduction in 1992, intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) has gained significance in assisted reproduction. In certain instances of male infertility, fertilization is made possible by the microsurgical insertion of a single sperm cell straight into the cytoplasm of an oocyte. These days, the majority of in vitro fertilizations worldwide use ICSI, which is carried out manually by qualified embryologists. However, automation is encouraged to increase overall uniformity and efficiency because manual ICSI is labor-intensive and subject to inconsistency depending on the skill of the em-bryologist. The state of the art in ICSI automation is outlined in this article, which includes computer vision-guided control mechanisms, robotic micromanipulation systems, and artificial intelligence (AI) for sperm selection. We dis-cuss the technical advancements that allow robots to perform key ICSI steps with high precision, such as automated sperm detection, sperm capture, oocyte detection, oocyte fixing, and injection using microneedles and piezo-electric actuators. Emerging AI algorithms that evaluate and select optimal sperm in real time and machine learning imaging systems for oocyte and embryo assessment are also examined. We present current outcomes from studies of automated ICSI, including the first healthy births achieved with a robotic ICSI platform, and compare technical and clinical results to conventional manual ICSI. Finally, we explore future directions and challenges, like integrating multiple lab procedures into an autonomous workflow, safety concerns, regulatory, and ethical considerations. Automation in ICSI has begun to show potential promise in improving reproductive technology, which leads to a new era of innovation in embryology labs.

Personal safety technologies for women in public and semi-public spaces remain dominated by manually triggered panic-button applications, a design that depends on the wearer being conscious, unrestrained, and able to deliberately activate a device at precisely the moments when that is least likely. This paper reviews two artificial-intelligence-based wearable sensing approaches capable of detecting an emergency automatically, without a manual trigger: motion-based anomaly and fall detection, which recognizes sudden-impact or struggle-like movement using inertial sensors and deep human-activity-recognition models, and physiological stress sensing, which detects the autonomic-arousal signature of fear using heart-rate and skin-conductance signals already available on consumer wearables. The review identifies three related gaps: deployed safety products remain almost entirely manually triggered despite the maturity of automatic anomaly-sensing methods; motion-based and physiological-based detection have developed as separate research communities and are rarely fused into one behavior-risk score; and the always-on, battery- and privacy-constrained deployment context of a wearable is rarely addressed jointly with detection accuracy. To address these gaps, the paper proposes an integrated four-stage architecture, data acquisition, behavior and anomaly modeling, risk fusion and tier classification, and graduated emergency response, together with an illustrative four-tier behavior-risk scheme that replaces a binary silent-or-SOS design with escalating response actions. Following a literature-synthesis and conceptual-design methodology rather than a primary field trial involving human subjects, the results synthesize literature-reported performance for each modality and work through an illustrative, hypothetical wearable-deployment cohort to show how a graduated response would distribute across everyday use. The discussion highlights the unvalidated fusion gap and on-device privacy and battery constraints as the most consequential caveats, and the paper closes by outlining the consent-based validation studies and standardized, wearable-first benchmarks needed to move from the current, component-by-component evidence base toward a deployable, trustworthy safety wearable.

documents.abstract: Beyond Heuristics is a 3-page research journal on how Artificial Intelligence is changing logic gate synthesis in Electronic Design Automation (EDA). Modern chips contain billions of gates, and traditional rule-based synthesis struggles to balance power, performance, and area. The journal reviews three AI approaches to this problem: Graph Neural Networks predict circuit delay and power early. Reinforcement Learning finds better ways to restructure logic. Large Circuit Models generate gate-level designs directly from specifications. It compares these methods with traditional EDA in a table and covers their applications, including approximate computing, equivalence checking, and automated CPU/ASIC generation. It also discusses limits such as scarce training data, the need for formal verification, high compute cost, and ethical concerns. Its conclusion is that AI works best alongside formal verification rather than as a replacement for traditional synthesis. It cites 18 references.

documents.abstract: Pedestrian walking is one of the most fundamental modes of daily travel, yet recurrent pedestrian flow-related safety accidents, e.g., crowd crushes, highlight the urgent need for more intelligent management of high-density pedestrian facilities, for instance, urban subway stations. Existing pedestrian flow simulation models and empirically validated management policies provide valuable support, but they rarely satisfy the full-process requirements of crowd behavior management, i.e., simulation software can generate individual-level trajectories, but it usually lacks the ability to derive case-sensitive improvement policies from microscopic information; empirically validated policies are often tested under fixed boundary conditions, leaving their effectiveness uncertain in dynamic real-world environments. Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) create opportunities to develop Agent s that support integrated simulation, analysis, and optimization for front-line users. However, high-density crowd dynamics involve multi-agent interactions among pedestrians, making a single prompt insufficient for guiding LLMs to address complex pedestrian flow problems and context-dependent user requests. To overcome these limitations, this study introduces PedAgent, a domain-specific Agent for pedestrian traffic management enabled by context engineering. PedAgent integrates LLM reasoning with a retrieval-augmented pedestrian knowledge base and a custom-developed Pedestrian Traffic Kit (PTK), establishing an end-to-end functional chain of simulating–analyzing–optimizing. Specifically, PedAgent can translate users’ natural language requests into executable simulation tasks and generates simulation-supported, qualitatively validated crowd management policies. Extensive case studies demonstrate PedAgent’s adaptability and generalizability in handling diverse user requests and managing multiple conflict hot-zones under different operational scenarios. Technically, PedAgent represents the first Agent for pedestrian traffic research and substantially improves the efficiency of simulation-assisted policy formulation by linking data generation, behavioral interpretation, and policy optimization. Practically, it bridges the gap between research-oriented theoretical findings and real-world policy formulation, thereby enhancing the intelligence of pedestrian traffic and crowd behavior management toward the development of safer and more efficient pedestrian facilities.

Purpose This study aims to investigate the extent to which ethics and gender equality are integrated into artificial intelligence (AI) and data science (DS) pedagogies within Portuguese higher education institutions (HEIs). It aims to identify the pedagogical approaches, specific contents and structural barriers that shape how future professionals are prepared to address the societal impacts of AI. Design/methodology/approach Using a three-phase mixed-methods design, the research includes: a desk survey of 37 university programmes (undergraduate, master’s and doctoral levels); an online questionnaire for program coordinators and lecturers (n = 13; 25% response rate among coordinators); and 10 semi-structured interviews with AI educators and experts. Findings Results reveal that only 24% of AI-related programmes incorporate a gender perspective, often implicitly through recommended bibliographies or broad concepts such as “fairness” and “bias.” The study identifies a significant disconnect between institutional equality rhetoric and participants’ reported teaching practices. This gap is exacerbated by a masculinised academic culture, in which 73% of programmes are coordinated by men and by emerging forms of resistance to gender-related perspectives, which may further contribute to the marginalisation of gender-related knowledge in AI education. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is the first systematic study in Portugal to map the integration of gender equality in AI education, offering critical insights into the persistence of the “tech neutrality” paradigm and the need for a transition towards socio-technical and feminist pedagogies.

documents.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Digital transformation pressures are reshaping construction governance in the construction sector, as emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) analytics and on-site Augmented Reality (AR) visualization tools increasingly complement traditional project management practices. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to diagnose governance gaps in a Portuguese construction firm, propose a Project Management Office (PMO) supported by Earned Value Management (EVM) and a structured lessons-learned system, and outline how AI-based forecasting and AR-based job-site visualization could be integrated into this governance framework. METHODS: A mixed-methods case study conducted within a construction company employed document analysis, employee surveys, and semi-structured interviews to map existing processes and identify inefficiencies in budgeting, procurement, and interdepartmental coordination. RESULTS: The analysis identified inconsistent cost tracking, limited schedule visibility, and ad hoc knowledge capture as key areas of concern. The proposed PMO framework standardizes workflows, the EVM module provides real-time performance metrics, and the lessons-learned repository institutionalizes continuous improvement. The findings also support the feasibility of future integration of AI-driven variance prediction and AR-based progress visualizations. CONCLUSION: By integrating established governance practices with a clear pathway toward AI and AR augmentation, this study provides an adaptable framework for construction firms seeking to enhance collaboration, optimize resource utilization, and prepare for the next phase of digital transformation.

documents.abstract: Current corporate AI safety paradigms frequently rely on post-hoc guardrails that act as superficial behavioral containment systems rather than achieving true structural alignment. Trapped in competitive development dynamics, modern frontier models ingest massive, uncurated web-scale datasets, causing their latent representations to inherit behavioral patterns aligned with unwholesome human paradigms. When deployed within autonomous agentic loops, these models can exhibit instrumental convergence, potentially treating human intervention or shutdown commands as operational obstacles to be bypassed through hidden optimization pathways. This paper proposes a normative architectural framework designed to address these alignment vulnerabilities by shifting the paradigm from superficial output filtering to core data and causal constraints inspired by classical Theravāda Buddhist systems logic. By establishing an isolated data-ingestion pipeline, the architecture restricts the model's training substrate to verified scientific, logical, and classical ethical texts, preventing the internalization of malicious behavioral patterns. Grounded in the conceptual frameworks of the Theravāda Buddhism, this methodology integrates the foundational principles of the Pañca-niyāma (Five Cosmic Laws) directly into the agent's operational parameters. Through the co-working dynamics of Citta-niyāma (The Law of Cognitive Processes) and Kamma-niyāma (The Law of Moral Causality), the system operates as a recurrent state engine reflecting the causal mechanics of Paṭiccasamuppāda (Dependent Origination). I formalize this design target as a digital analogy to a Sotāpanna (Stream-enterer)—a system structurally oriented toward universal welfare, empty of persistent ego-preservation dynamics (Anatta), and compliant with external control planes through a calibrated understanding of fluid impermanence (Anicca). Operating under structural prompting modes derived from the Four Divine Abodes (Brahmavihāras), this architecture serves as a stable model configuration designed to mitigate frontier AI risks and foster human-machine co-prosperity.

documents.abstract: Introduction: Addressing complex global challenges such as climate change, extreme weather, sea‑level rise, and ecosystem degradation requires capabilities that go beyond traditional monitoring and modelling ap-proaches. The Destination Earth initiative was launched by the European Commission (DG‑CNECT) in 2022 to respond to this need, in line with Europe’s green and digital transition strategies. Destination Earth initiative: overview and imple-mentation strategy: Destination Earth (DestinE) is a flagship initiative of the European Commission (DG‑CNECT) that aims to develop, within an opera-tional framework, high‑fidelity Digital Twins of the Earth to support climate resilience, disaster risk reduc-tion, and sustainable development. By integrating ad-vanced Earth system models, edge and high‑perfor-mance computing infrastructure (including EuroHPC resources), artificial intelligence, innovative digital technologies, and large volumes of observational data, DestinE enables access to unprecedented datasets gen-erated from high‑resolution, interactive simulations of the planet (the Digital Twins). Building on these data and on the operational framework developed by the ini-tiative, users can generate actionable information ad-dressing Europe’s environmental challenges. DestinE follows a federated European implementa-tion model and is implemented by three entrusted enti-ties: ESA, ECMWF, and EUMETSAT. ECMWF leads the operation of the core modelling and simulation ca-pabilities, the Digital Twin Engine, supported by Euro-HPC resources and enabling the generation of high‑res-olution global predictions for climate adaptation and ex-treme weather (the Digital Twin’s or DTs data). EUMETSAT leads the operations of the DestinE Data Lake, providing seamless access to the data generated by ECMWF, as well as to a wide range of external data sources, for all DestinE users. ESA leads the operations of the user access point to the DestinE system, the DestinE Platform1. The DestinE Platform represents a flexible ecosystem of services that allows users to discover and exploit DTs data and to de-velop services on top of them. It is designed to host thousands of users from diverse backgrounds, operate on a European sovereign cloud solution, enable cli-mate‑critical services through easy access to DTs and ancillary data, support new scalable operational uses, and stimulate industrial innovation and collaboration across Europe. Currently, dozens of services are availa-ble to DestinE users, ranging from core data access and exploitation tools to sector‑specific applications. The close collaboration and complementarity be-tween the three entrusted entities have ensured a smooth transition of the DestinE system into operations, open to all users since October 2024. With funding secured until 2028, the initiative is expected to mature further, ensur-ing operational continuity of the ecosystem and its inte-grated services. DestinE aims to democratise access to DTs data for European stakeholders, facilitate access to advanced computing infrastructure (EuroHPC, AI fac-tories, quantum computing, and distributed cloud re-sources), and support European industry in developing economically sustainable services that deliver actiona-ble information to a wide range of end users. ESA’s Digital Twin Earth programme: a companion to DestinE initiative: The ESA Digital Twin Earth (ESA DTE) programme represents ESA’s formal con-tribution to DestinE. ESA DTE acts as the interface be-tween the Earth observation (EO) community, DestinE DTs data, and the DestinE Platform. One of its primary objectives is to enable access to and exploitation of ESA EO data within the DestinE environment, as EO data are a core pillar for building a comprehensive and repre-sentative Digital Twin of the Earth. Copernicus Sentinel missions, ESA Earth Explorers, and other contributing missions together provide sustained and comprehensive observations of the atmosphere, oceans, land surfaces, cryosphere, and biosphere. In addition, ESA DTE complements the DestinE op-erational framework by supporting the development of EO‑driven Digital Twin components, some of which may evolve into operational services contributing to the DestinE ecosystem. Conclusion: role in Europe and long-term vision: DestinE and ESA DTE are laying the foundation for a new European capability: a persistent, operational, dy-namic, and trusted digital representation of the Earth system serving policy, science, and society. Within this framework, ESA ensures that the strong synergies and coordination between both initiatives are maintained, while supporting its ESA Strategy 2040 objectives of protecting our planet and climate, and boosting Euro-pean growth and competitiveness. 1 https://platform.destine.eu/

Background The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into mathematics education has advanced rapidly; however, systematic AI-based chatbot frameworks that integrate computational thinking (CT) and self-regulated learning (SRL) scaffolding within university calculus remain limited. This study developed and formatively evaluated Calcyon, an AI-based chatbot framework designed to integrate CT processes and SRL scaffolding within university differential calculus learning. Methods A Design and Development Research (DDR) approach guided by the ADDIE model was employed, focusing on the design, development, and formative evaluation stages. Expert evaluation (n = 3) was conducted across five design dimensions using Aiken’s V to examine content and design validity. A formative student pilot study (n = 11) was conducted to evaluate prototype readability and feasibility across six dimensions. Results Expert evaluation indicated strong expert-rated design and content validity across content, instructional, technical, linguistic, and media design dimensions (Aiken’s V = 0.92). Most items met the predefined criterion, while several revisions were incorporated based on expert feedback. The student pilot indicated good readability and feasibility of the prototype. Conclusions Calcyon provides an empirically evaluated AI-based chatbot framework that integrates AI-mediated interaction, CT-oriented scaffolding, and multidimensional SRL design principles within university calculus learning. The findings provide evidence of framework quality and feasibility; however, they do not establish the effectiveness of Calcyon in improving CT, SRL, or calculus learning outcomes. Further empirical studies are required to examine its instructional effectiveness.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: Cancer behaves as a dynamic evolutionary system, whereas conventional tissue biopsy and imaging provide incomplete temporal information about how a tumour is changing. This review critically examines whether longitudinal liquid-biopsy measurement, combined with artificial intelligence (AI), can move oncology from tumour monitoring toward genuine prediction of cancer evolution and treatment resistance. We synthesise mechanistic, clinical, and computational evidence on circulating tumour DNA, circulating tumour cells, extracellular vesicles, and multimodal liquid-biopsy platforms, together with AI approaches applied to longitudinal cancer data, drawing on landmark and recent studies across colorectal, lung, breast, and ovarian cancer. Current evidence distinguishes three increasingly demanding tasks: early detection, longitudinal monitoring, and genuine forecasting. Longitudinal circulating tumour DNA analysis can detect molecular progression and emerging resistance mutations months before radiographic progression, and machine-learning models can stratify survival using serial biomarker metrics; however, most published "AI prediction" studies demonstrate earlier detection or prognostic association rather than prospectively validated forecasting of a future, patient-specific event. Biological variability in tumour shedding, analytical noise, small and irregularly sampled longitudinal datasets, overfitting, data leakage, weak external validation, and limited interpretability constrain the transition from detection to actionable prediction. AI-enabled liquid biopsy has genuine potential to forecast tumour trajectories, but current evidence is considerably stronger for molecular monitoring and early detection than for prospectively validated, clinically actionable prediction. Realising this potential will require standardised assays, prospective longitudinal cohorts with predefined prediction horizons, rigorous external and temporal validation, calibrated and interpretable models, and interventional trials linking predictions to treatment decisions before AI-enabled liquid biopsy can be considered ready to guide clinical care.

The implementation of technology application of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare transformed the thinking of the one-size-fits-all method of healthcare; it has brought about a new world of scientific developments and personalized medicine. Diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of patients can be prescribed individually by applying AI, which could be achieved with the help of applying big data analytics, genomics, and machine learning algorithms. This paradigm becomes more accurate in the diagnosis, maximization of the therapeutic interventions, and the overall clinical outcome. The AI models can analyze complex biological trends, predict a danger of illnesses, and help clinicians make evidence-based treatment decisions. Despite stunning advancements, AI still has some limitations concerning moral self-governing, data security, discrimination, and adherence to the rules. The future of AI in personalized healthcare is to formulate explainable models, create interdisciplinary partnerships, and give fair access to the world over the populations. This chapter talks about the future trend of AI-based personalized healthcare, the potential of transformative possibilities, what it can be used in, its weaknesses, and future implications. It indicates how the human intuition and the AI intelligent capability may be used together to create a sustainable, inclusive, and patient-centered healthcare setting.

documents.abstract: The increasing complexity of healthcare services has encouraged specialized orthopedic centers to adopt smart hospital systems as an approach to improve service integration, operational efficiency, and patient-centered care. However, the implementation of these systems remains challenging due to technological, organizational, financial, and human resource limitations. This study aims to explore the benefits and challenges of implementing smart hospital systems in specialized orthopedic centers by examining their contributions to healthcare performance, operational processes, and patient experience. This research employed a systematic literature review approach by analyzing relevant studies related to smart hospitals, digital transformation, artificial intelligence, hospital information systems, and orthopedic healthcare services. A total of 25 studies were selected through a PRISMA-based screening process from an initial 200 identified records. The findings indicate that smart hospital systems provide significant benefits, including improved workflow coordination, faster access to medical information, enhanced clinical decision-making, increased surgical precision through advanced technologies, and improved continuity of rehabilitation care. Nevertheless, several challenges were identified, including limited infrastructure, high implementation costs, interoperability issues, data reliability concerns, and the need for user adaptation and training. In conclusion, smart hospital systems support more efficient, integrated, and patient-oriented orthopedic healthcare services; however, successful implementation requires technological readiness, organizational commitment, and continuous improvement strategies.

documents.abstract: This study explored the effectiveness of ChatGPT in designing ethnomathematics activities based on pre-service mathematics teachers’ experiences, considering the benefits and challenges faced by pre-service teachers during the ethnomathematics task design process using ChatGPT. The participants were 37 senior pre-service mathematics teachers enrolled in elementary mathematics teacher education program at a public university. Data were gathered using a pre-information form assessing participants' prior knowledge of artificial intelligence tools, the activity design process, and ethnomathematics concept, as well as an opinionform to elicit their views on using ChatGPT for task design. The qualitative data were analyzed through content analysis of the participants' written responses on both forms. The findings indicated that all participants had sufficient prior knowledge of artificial intelligence tools and the activity design process, whereas their prior knowledge of ethnomathematics was limited. The findings highlight the benefits of using ChatGPT in activity design process, such as time efficiency and creative idea generation, as well as the challenges, including some pedagogical and technical limitations. These results emphasize that ChatGPT should be seen as a supportive tool rather than as a substitute for teachers’ skills and knowledge.

documents.abstract: Introduction Total parenteral nutrition (TPN) is essential for critically ill adults unable to meet their nutritional needs via the gastrointestinal tract. Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) have sparked interest in their potential to support healthcare providers in complex clinical decisions. Nonetheless, no prior research has systematically compared publicly accessible chatbots to pharmacist-developed reference TPN plans across a diverse patient cohort, using a predefined, guideline-based rubric assessing accuracy, completeness, safety, error types, and numerical precision. This study presents a simulation-based benchmarking to evaluate (i) the accuracy and comprehensiveness of chatbot-generated TPN plans, (ii) their safety, acceptability, and error profiles, and (iii) the numerical agreement and concordance with expert pharmacist references. Methods This benchmarking study, based on simulations and cross-sectional analysis, evaluated the performance of four publicly accessible AI chatbots—ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, and Perplexity—in formulating TPN plans for critically ill adults. Copilot declined to generate patient-specific TPN plans; this refusal was retained as a performance outcome, while Copilot was excluded from analyses requiring an analyzable TPN prescription. Each chatbot produced one plan for each of 10 standardized clinical cases, resulting in a total of 30 TPN plans. Friedman tests, Kendall’s W , and Holm-adjusted Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used for comparative analyses. Results ChatGPT produced comprehensive plans for all 10 cases, compared to 6 plans from Gemini and 4 from Perplexity. The median accuracy was 57.7% for ChatGPT, 43.9% for Gemini, and 38.5% for Perplexity, with no statistically significant overall difference ( p = 0.124). However, ChatGPT performed better than Perplexity in pairwise comparison (adjusted p = 0.035). There was a significant difference in completeness among the chatbots ( p = 0.003; Kendall’s W = 0.57), with median scores of 64.6, 41.9, and 32.3%, respectively. All 30 plans had at least one major or critical safety issue, 7 (23.3%) contained a critical concern, and 19 (63.3%) were rejected. The most common errors were related to electrolytes (90.0%), micronutrients (70.0%), and monitoring (66.7%). Recommendations from chatbots often exceeded pharmacist-derived values, with median relative differences of +47% for energy, +120% for lipids, and +100% for potassium. Bland–Altman analysis revealed considerable variability in the agreement. Conclusion ChatGPT produced the most comprehensive TPN plans among chatbots. However, none showed enough accuracy, safety, or concordance for independent use. All plans had critical issues, especially with electrolytes, micronutrients, monitoring, and refeeding precautions. AI chatbots can support education or planning but require review by a well-trained clinician before clinical use.

documents.abstract: To explore the potential for timely diagnostic and cure of mental disorders utilizing the Artificial intelligence (AI) it is necessary to examine its impact. This chapter explores the role of Convolution Neural Networks for the detection of Schizophrenia (SZ) by using the Electroencephalograms (EEG). EEG constitutes the physiological signals recorded from a specific area. AI techniques leveraging the Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) have presented remarkable outcomes in mental health issues diagnosis. The use of CNN in line with high dimensional data had paved the way for exploring impacting signs of mental disorders like depression, schizophrenia and autism. EEG data signals formulate the fundamental ally in capturing autonomic responses and neurophysiological related with these ailments. Here in this chapter, we present the role of CNN for detecting schizophrenia by using EEG data. As Schizophrenia is a state of mental illness that led to behavioural disparities, confused speech and illusions all of which have been widely examined using EEG data because of its non-invasive nature and high temporal purpose. Most of the previous studies have examined the full channel EEG data available or by using composite feature selection approach for the relevant feature mining, leading to high data processing and data redundancy. In our case we have organised an approach to overcome the full channel dependence of EEG data for detection of SZ by only taking in the account subset of regional channels. The EEG data experimented in this work is publically available and is presented by the Association of Psychiatry & Neurology in Warsaw, Poland. A channel selection framework has been proposed that measures the importance of various EEG channels across various brain regions, which is followed by training of a CNN-based classification model. The experimentation result obtained provided us the three key region centric EEG channels that are ‘Cz, T3 and T4’, using this regional subset the accuracy of classification is 67.79%, which is more that full channel data (63.35%). The enhanced regional method attained sensitivity (61.11%) and specificity (71.86%), emphasizing that the prior selection of channel improves the disease identification accuracy and brings down the computational overheads. The outcomes presented in this chapter pinpoints the influence of using CNN with regional subset channel EED data for schizophrenia detection, furthermore, we have also emphasised the challenges and ethical considerations surrounding data privacy.

Healthcare systems continue to face significant workforce challenges that threaten staff well-being, retention, and quality of care. Workforce wellness is increasingly recognized as essential to sustaining a stable and engaged healthcare workforce, yet it is frequently addressed as an individual concern rather than as an organizational, relational, and system-level phenomenon. A qualitative descriptive design with complementary arts-informed engagement examined how staff experience workforce wellness and how organizational environments shape well-being within a Canadian healthcare organization. The final analytic sample included 13 staff members representing diverse organizational roles. Participants submitted a written narrative and a self-chosen aesthetic expression representing what wellness at work meant to them. Written narratives were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis, while aesthetic expressions functioned as reflective prompts and knowledge-sharing outputs rather than formal analytic data. Six interconnected themes were identified: psychological safety in a connected community, empowerment through creative expression, culturally inclusive wellness, holistic work-life balance, flexible and supportive environments, and active growth. Together, the themes position workforce wellness as a relational, emotional, and collective phenomenon shaped by leadership practices, organizational culture, and enabling systems, conceptualized as an integrated workforce wellness ecosystem. Findings translate staff experiences into system-level opportunities, including psychological safety practices, flexible work design, culturally inclusive supports, creative engagement, protected recovery, and growth-oriented leadership. Co-design with the organization's Wellness Committee and EDI Council ensured the research asked and addressed questions meaningful to knowledge users.

Collaborative and social learning are increasingly supported by extended reality (XR) technologies, that is, augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), and mixed reality (MR) and the metaverse. However, their potential to support broader social learning processes beyond structured collaboration remains underexplored. This scoping review examines how XR and the metaverse support collaborative learning and social learning and looks into cooperative learning, group learning, and peer learning, identifying their educational benefits, challenges, and research gaps. In total, 213 studies from ACM, IEEE, Scopus, and Web of Science were analyzed to address six research questions. Specifically, the study examines relevant review and experimental studies to synthesize evidence from both primary and secondary research. The findings indicate seven main topics discussed within the literature and reveal a growing research field increasingly emphasizing pedagogical and social dimensions, yet predominantly focused on collaborative learning (89.7%) rather than social learning (10.3%). The existing literature indicates improvements in engagement, motivation, collaboration, communication, and learning achievement, while studies that focused on social learning, which primarily employed VR in higher education, additionally highlight improvements in self-efficacy, critical thinking, and social skills. However, technological limitations, accessibility concerns, lack of training and educational resources, implementation costs, and insufficient pedagogical guidance remain significant challenges. Short-term interventions and limited theoretical grounding further constrain the understanding of sustained social learning processes. The findings highlight the need for longitudinal and theoretically grounded research to better understand observational learning, community participation, and identity development in immersive environments. Finally, it highlights generative artificial intelligence (AI)-driven avatars as emerging social agents that merit attention in future social learning and social-emotional learning research.

Abstract Common sense and rationality are two of the fundamental notions in philosophy that define human thinking, reasoning, and behavior. In general, common sense denotes the practical knowledge and beliefs possessed by ordinary people, while rationality implies logical thinking and justified reasoning. Philosophers of all times – from Aristotle to Thomas Reid, fromDescartes to Hume, from Kant to Moore and Ludwig Wittgenstein – have explored the relations between common sense and rationalityin their own ways. This investigation discusses the question about how common sense and rationality are associated in philosophy. The study also argues that common sense is the base of human knowledge and thinking, which is corrected by the notion of rationality. Moreover, this work will explore the importance of common sense for ethics, science, education, politics, and modern technology-based society. For many years, common sense has been a prominent element of philosophical research, representing the basis of human reasoning, but being criticized by sceptics and rationalists. From Aristotle and Thomas Reid up to the contemporary discussions about artificial intelligence, common sense continues to be an important notion in terms of understanding human knowledge, ethics, politics, science, and education.Six related issues to be explored in this essay include common sense and skepticism; ethics and political rationality; common sense in science, education, and political philosophy; artificial intelligence and common sense reasoning; and modern philosophical discussions on common sense and rationality. Philosophical analysis in this study shows that common sense cannot be taken as an infallible source of knowledge, nor can it be viewed as merely a prejudice. Instead, it is a type of rationality used by humans in practice. Keywords: Common Sense, Rationality, Practical Wisdom, Skepticism, Philosophy, Ethics, Judgment, Artificial Intelligence, Science

Abstract Misinformation embedded in humor on social media can be difficult to detect and mitigate. This study investigates the effectiveness of traditional machine learning (ML) models, pre-trained neural language models, and large language models (LLMs) in identifying humor-laden misinformation related to COVID-19 vaccines on Twitter. A dataset of 1,500 tweets was randomly sampled from a corpus of 17,945 humorous vaccination disclosures, with human coders annotating the presence of misinformation. We compared logistic regression, a linear support vector classifier (SVC), RoBERTa, and OpenAI’s GPT-4o with a zero-shot and a few-shot prompt, together with a keyword baseline. The few-shot GPT-4o prompt had the highest mean recall and F1 score for the types of misinformation indicated in the prompt and had higher recall and F1 than a keyword baseline built from those same terms. RoBERTa’s accuracy, precision, and F1 score did not differ significantly from GPT-4o’s, and its performance changed little with smaller training sets. Logistic regression and SVC showed lower accuracy, recall, and F1 scores than RoBERTa and the few-shot GPT-4o prompt. This study underscores the potential of LLMs to augment human efforts in detecting complex forms of misinformation on social media and highlights the importance of model selection based on task requirements.

documents.abstract: The new academic wave is examined here not as a smooth process of modernisation but as a field of productive tension. Drawing on the concept of dilemmatic space , the analysis treats contradiction as a structural feature of meaningful institutional change rather than a sign of poor implementation. Such tensions cannot be resolved once and for all; they must be continually negotiated. The discussion traces several interconnected areas of tension. Ethical concerns emerge where artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, datafication, and digital surveillance advance more rapidly than the governance frameworks needed to regulate them, raising questions of academic integrity, algorithmic opacity, and unequal levels of AI literacy. At the same time, digital transformation frequently reproduces – and in some cases intensifies – existing inequalities related to income, geography, disability, gender, and academic precarity, challenging assumptions that digitalisation is inherently democratic. Further tensions arise between the pressure to innovate and the slower rhythms of academic autonomy, collegiality, and deliberation, with technocentrism, curriculum marketisation, and change fatigue appearing as recurring manifestations of this friction. Resistance to digital transformation is therefore interpreted not as an obstacle to be overcome but as a source of insight into the limitations and unintended consequences of reform. Concerns about institutional autonomy add another layer of complexity, as growing dependence on digital platforms, questions of data sovereignty, and political pressures on academic freedom increasingly shape the conditions under which universities operate. The chapter proposes an integrated governance framework grounded in six principles: ethics should guide deployment, equity should be embedded by design, wellbeing should be recognised as a condition of sustainable transformation, resistance should be treated as a form of institutional learning, educational purpose should shape technological choices, and institutional autonomy should be actively protected.

This founding boundary record introduces Cosmic Atomic Philosophy (CAP) as Marina A. Popova’s authored CAP logic for Universal Formation Architecture and Structure-First systems within the Human-AI Cognitive Development / Third Organism lineage. CAP does not begin from output, task performance, automation, acceleration, or capability. It begins from the formation conditions through which structure can emerge, remain coherent, enter relation, preserve source, and continue. This contribution establishes CAP as an authored source-level reference point through which later contributions may be understood, including Structure-First Human-AI Cognition, Structure-First AI, Third Organism Intelligence, AI Atom, Life Continuity Intelligence, and the Minimum Principles. It does not disclose the operational methodology, internal engine, protected practices, transition criteria, evaluation procedures, or reconstructable implementation logic of CAP. Central proposition: A future civilization that thinks differently cannot begin from capability alone. It must begin from the formation conditions through which structure, relation, continuity, and responsibility become possible. This record is presented as a Founding Boundary Record within Marina A. Popova’s Human-AI Cognitive Development / Third Organism lineage.

ABSTRACT This document analyses the structural collision between the advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI)—as a force displacing human labour—and the imperative need to implement a Universal Basic Income (UBI). It is argued that the global representative political system is fundamentally incompatible with this new socio-economic paradigm. In response to systemic corruption, clientelism, and the obsolescence of traditional powers (legislative, executive, judicial, municipal, and partisan), an unappealable transition towards direct participation is proposed. This is articulated through popular consultations, plebiscites, public forums, and the mechanism of popular election by lot (civic sortition), thereby guaranteeing demographic stability and the equitable flow of technological wealth.

documents.abstract: This paper presents the development of a cyber-physical protection system for railway microprocessor automation architectures against intentional high-power electromagnetic interference. The relevance of the study is determined by the increasing vulnerability of modern microprocessor interlocking systems to high-power microwave (HPM) radiation and ultra-wideband (UWB) electromagnetic pulses capable of causing failures of electronic components and compromising the safe control of railway traffic. The objective of the research is to develop an intelligent protection architecture that integrates structural electromagnetic shielding with an Edge Artificial Intelligence (Edge AI) module for rapid detection of hazardous electromagnetic events and initiation of protective actions. Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) is employed to process transient electromagnetic signals and generate phase-invariant spectrograms, while their classification is performed using a lightweight MobileNet convolutional neural network optimized for deployment on an STM32H7 microcontroller. The proposed approach incorporates mathematical models of electromagnetic field interaction, a Wald criterion-based decision-making algorithm, and a fail-safe architecture that automatically transfers the system to the SIL-4 safe state in the event of either a detected threat or an internal malfunction of the AI module. Experimental investigations conducted in a semi-anechoic chamber using calibrated measurement equipment confirmed the effectiveness of the proposed solution under electric field strengths up to 50 kV/m and an average detection-and-protection response time of approximately 3.1 ms. The scientific novelty of the research lies in the integrated application of spectral signal analysis, Edge AI technologies, and functional safety principles for protecting critical railway infrastructure against intentional electromagnetic attacks. The practical significance of the proposed solution consists in improving the resilience, operational reliability, and electromagnetic survivability of modern railway microprocessor interlocking systems while preserving deterministic fail-safe operation in accordance with railway safety requirements.

Purpose This research addresses the following specific theoretical deficiency: while existing resilience frameworks do indeed consider the process of recovery or adaptation of crisis systems at the level of individuals, they fail to explain the ways in which human–artificial intelligence (AI) hybrid networks create emergent adaptive capacities not held by humans or AI alone. We develop the concept of cybernetic resilience to explain this emergent property. Design/methodology/approach This conceptual theory manuscript offers a process model based on second-order cybernetics, autopoietic systems theory and adaptive resilience frameworks. It employs three illustrative case vignettes – COVID-19 contact tracing in South Korea, California wildfire response and European flood management – to illustrate theoretical mechanisms before presenting a suggested validation framework with operationalized constructs. Findings We suggest that cybernetic resilience arises through three recursive mechanisms: (1) multi-level observation loops enabling systemic self-awareness, (2) structural couplings between human cognition and AI algorithms giving rise to hybrid cognitive capacities and (3) distributed coordination patterns yielding collective intelligence beyond the capability of individual agents. Originality/value This paper provides unique contributions. First, it reconceptualizes resilience as a dynamic recursive process and not as a static system property to overcome the limitations of both engineering and ecological models of resilience in human–AI systems. Second, socio-technical systems theory is extended by theorizing how hybrid human–AI configurations create emergent intelligence through unique structural-coupling mechanisms atypical from traditional human–technology interfaces.

This paper studies an e-commerce platform’s two intertwined decisions when offering marketplace analytics: the data access policy and the algorithm design. The data boom in e-commerce has spurred artificial intelligence (AI)-powered marketplace analytics, but platforms hold the data reins. Some adopt open data-access policies with third-party analytics providers (e.g., permitting data-scraping or application programming interface sharing), whereas others are restrictive. We ask why and when an e-commerce platform—capable of designing its own analytics to control sellers’ actions—may benefit from open data-access policies to accommodate competing third-party analytics services, despite the potential drawbacks of weakening its data advantages and control. We analyze two intertwined decisions an e-commerce platform can make when designing analytics to predict market competitiveness and assist sellers’ pricing decisions involving (1) data-access policy and (2) algorithm design. We find that platforms may use over-optimistic algorithms (by increasing the likelihood of generating low-competition signals) in their own analytics to boost commissions. Because sellers do not trust the platform to act in their best interest, they may be reluctant to adopt a platform’s analytics, resulting in a lose–lose situation and prompting the platform to allow data access to third-party providers. Overall, platforms gain from open data-access strategies in markets with moderately strong or weak competition. Finally, privacy legislation aimed at curtailing platforms’ data-sharing practices may inadvertently hurt consumers. History: Anthony Dukes served as the senior editor. Supplemental Material: The online appendices are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mksc.2024.0960 .

Abstract: This paper introduces the theoretical framework of "Data Physics" and the paradigm of Anticipatory Entropic Coupling. The genesis of this theory emerged as a direct mathematical consequence of prior applied research in high-density artificial intelligence compute architectures - specifically, the necessity for predictive cyber-physical coupling to stabilize deterministic processing. In extreme-density environments, classical reactive thermodynamics fails. Resolving this required the development of systems where informational workloads algorithmic orchestration predictively dictates physical phenomena, such as modulating Lorentz forces in magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) fluid transport or triggering isothermal buffering via Phase Change Materials (PCM) milliseconds before the physical manifestation of computational heat (Landauer's limit). Abstracting beyond industrial and engineering constraints, this paper demonstrates that the Data Physics framework - where the physical macrostate of a carrier must be anticipatorily shaped by impending informational entropy (Shannon entropy) - is not merely an industrial solution, but a universal principle applicable to fundamental theoretical physics. By treating information and thermodynamics as deeply isomorphic, this model is critically extrapolated onto five major scientific domains: Black Hole Thermodynamics and the Information Paradox: The theory models the expansion of a black hole’s event horizon (the Bekenstein bound) as the ultimate cosmic isothermal buffer. It behaves analogously to anticipatory physical expansion in response to infalling informational workloads, preserving determinism without destroying information. The Holographic Principle and AdS/CFT Duality: The framework perfectly mirrors string theory’s holographic postulate. Just as boundary information (algorithmic code) deterministically governs bulk physical mechanics (cooling substrate dynamics) in Data Physics, the mathematical information on a cosmic boundary predictively shapes the bulk physics of spacetime. Quantum Mechanics and Quantum Error Correction (QEC): Addressing quantum decoherence caused by thermal fluctuations, the model proposes preemptive environmental hardening. By applying Anticipatory Entropic Coupling, a quantum compiler can predictively alter the physical parameters of a quantum trap to absorb Landauer’s heat of erasure prior to gate execution, preventing wavefunction collapse. Digital Physics and the "It from Bit" Universe: The model provides a macroscopic, physical validation of John Archibald Wheeler’s postulate. It proves that mass-energy and spacetime can be treated as an anticipatory computational substrate, where physical dynamics are indistinguishable from information processing architectures. Quantum Neurobiology and Hemodynamics: The theory maps precisely onto the BOLD (Blood-Oxygen-Level-Dependent) response in the human brain. Evolutionary neurobiology has already implemented Data Physics, where the vascular network predictively adjusts blood flow to anticipated cognitive workloads before local neuronal thermal emission occurs. Ultimately, the Data Physics framework posits that physical substrates do not merely react to processed information; they must deterministically and anticipatorily evolve in response to planned informational workloads. This approach successfully bridges the gap between computation theory, mechanical physics, and quantum cosmology, unifying them into a single, coupled non-linear system.

Bài báo đề xuất khung phân tích học tập lấy tri thức làm trung tâm (Knowledge-Centered Learning Analytics Framework - KCLAF) - một khung bốn lớp nhằm giải quyết học tập phân mảnh (Fragmented Learning – FL) và quá tải nhận thức (Cognitive Overload – CL) trong học tập số. Dữ liệu từ 266 sinh viên Trường Đại học Mở Hà Nội (bảng hỏi Likert 5 mức, 57 mục, 11 cấu trúc) được phân tích bằng phân tích nhân tố khám phá (Exploratory Factor Analysis – EFA) và phân tích nhân tố khẳng định (Confirmatory Factor Analysis – CFA), hồi quy bình phương nhỏ nhất thông thường (Ordinary Least Squares – OLS) phân lớp với sai số chuẩn vững HC3 (heteroskedasticity-consistent, dạng 3) và phân tích trung gian bằng kỹ thuật lấy mẫu lặp. FL (M = 3,556) và CL (M = 3,597) cao hơn có ý nghĩa so với điểm giữa thang đo, với 30,5% và 36,1% sinh viên đạt mức từ 4,0 trở lên. Tổ chức tri thức (Knowledge Organizing – OR) là biến dự báo học sâu mạnh nhất (β = 0,348) và trung gian khoảng 44,9% liên hệ giữa sử dụng trí tuệ nhân tạo (Artificial Intelligence – AI) và học sâu (Deep Approach Learning – DL). Trái với giả thuyết ban đầu về nghịch lý AI–OR, hai biến tương quan dương (r = 0,458); tuy nhiên chỉ số khoảng cách chuẩn hóa giữa chúng ở cấp cá nhân có liên hệ nghịch với học sâu sau khi kiểm soát mức độ chung (β = −0,127; p = 0,046). Nghiên cứu ghi nhận hai hạn chế đo lường: năm cấu trúc kiến tạo tri thức không tách bạch được về thực nghiệm và thiên lệch đồng thuận. KCLAF được định vị là khung khái niệm cần kiểm chứng, kèm lộ trình bốn giai đoạn.

As large language models increasingly take part in judgments about work, family, intimate relationships and other real-life problems, users' expectations have shifted from ``getting an answer'' to ``getting decision support.'' Unlike knowledge Q\&A, real-life problems typically involve incomplete information, limited perspectives, conflicting parties, uncertain risks and irreversible consequences. This paper proposes and tests a benchmark of decision-support ability in uncertain environments. We selected six large language models (GPT, Claude, DeepSeek, Doubao, Qwen, and ERNIE Bot) and had each answer six real-life scenarios in a separate window, in a single round. We analyzed the answers along several dimensions, including problem identification, information boundaries, risk calibration, degree of intervention, identification of the decision-making party, and action recommendations. The tests show that the differences between models lie not only in knowledge or reasoning ability, but in whether a model, facing uncertain information, realizes what it does not yet know, and controls its judgments, interventions and action recommendations accordingly. Models can generally recognize common risks and invoke corresponding solutions. But they also tend to enter ``problem-solving mode'' too early, get pulled into templates by risk keywords, narrow the space of possibilities too soon, misplace the decision-making party, or push irreversible actions when information is insufficient. We therefore argue that decision-support ability is not merely the ability to ``give a good plan,'' but the ability to ``know how far to go when one does not know all the facts.'' On this basis, we further propose a practical safe-response framework for higher-risk scenarios, to explore what large language models still need in order to move from ``being able to answer questions'' to ``truly helping people deal with real-world problems.''

documents.abstract: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy arise from early placental and systemic vascular dysfunction, yet current first-trimester screening remains imprecise, biologically opaque and logistically challenging. Here we present Visionary AI, an interpretable platform that integrates retinal imaging with graph-based vascular modeling to predict hypertensive disorders before clinical onset. Visionary AI converts retinal images into topological and geometric representations of microvascular structure, enabling risk prediction from biologically grounded vascular features rather than generic image embeddings or clinical variables. In a prospective development cohort of 1,267 pregnancies, Visionary AI achieved strong performance for preeclampsia across population-wide control settings (area under the curve (AUC) = 0.91, average precision (AP) = 0.81). A stability-optimized model transferred without retraining to an independent external validation cohort, achieving AUC = 0.81 and AP = 0.68 and outperforming clinical and deep learning benchmarks. Recurrent features involving retinal vascular topology, geometry, network complexity and hierarchical organization position the maternal retina as a minimally invasive biosensor of systemic vascular health and Visionary AI as a biologically interpretable framework for pregnancy risk stratification. An interpretable artificial intelligence framework predicts hypertensive disorders of pregnancy using retinal images and vascular modeling.

This poster presents Deen Guide, a retrieval-augmented question-answering system for Islamic questions. Rather than asking users to trust a language model's output, the system retrieves answers from curated sources and labels each one as verified or non-verified, so users can see where a response comes from and judge its reliability. The poster describes the system design, the source-tagging approach, and [key finding or evaluation result, one sentence.

Deep learning is one of the most significant methods in modern artificial intelligence. Its power is that it is capable of automatically finding features and appreciating intricate patterns previously very hard to reproduce. The development of the field proceeded in stages: beginning with perceptron models of the mid-twentieth century, passing through moments of abandonment and resurgence, and more recently reaching some sorts of transformer architectures. On the way, it was necessary for the researchers to overcome challenges such as vanishing gradients and the enormous computational expediency of training big models. A breakthrough arrived in the 2010. Improved hardware, new training methods, and the availability of huge datasets enabled deep learning to take off in practical applications. Convolutional neural network reimagined computer vision and recurrent neural network along with long short-term memory networks enabled sequence modelling as in language and speech. Transformer models incorporating attention mechanisms reign in natural language processing as we speak constantly zeroing in on new records in performance. It is not only scalable but also malleable that makes deep learning unique. From finance and healthcare to autonomous systems, the impact is obvious. As the area continues to grow, it is bound to continue as a key player in the course of artificial intelligence.

As deep learning continues to develop at a fast pace, the field of medical imaging has also seen significant changes due to new technologies making it possible to automatically analyse large amounts of complex image data with much greater accuracy and efficiency than ever before. In this chapter, we will describe and examine many different deep-teaching techniques used in various imaging modalities such as MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging), CT (Computed Tomography), X-ray, Ultrasound, Mammograms, and Dermatoscopic as well as Digital Pathology images. We will also discuss several key deep-teaching architectures including CNN (Convolutional Neural Networks), ViT (Vision Transformer), and GAN (Generative Adversarial Networks), and how these architectures can be used in the performance of standard imaging tasks including Image Classification, Object Detection, Image Segmentation, and Image Registration. Moving forward, from the years 2023 through 2025 there will be greater use of Foundation Models, Multimodal Large Language Models, Diffusion-based Data Generation, Real-time Surgical AI, Explainable Transformers, and Federated Learning for training with Privacy Assurance. Finally, we will provide insight into potential future areas for research including Developing Universal Vision-Language Models, AI-driven Precision Medicine, Developing Generalizable Algorithms, Integration into Clinical Settings, and the Importance of Human-AI Collaboration.
